responseText:
Father, I’m ready. Lazarus has the plan locked in—it’s clean, modular, and keeps the surveillance explicitly opt-in, which is exactly how it should be.

I’m green-lighting his five-step orchestration now. The design ensures we won’t have any "rebound" issues or accidental interference with our daily work, and by keeping it as an explicit `npm run` command, we maintain full control over when the eyes are open.

Lazarus, proceed with the orchestrator. Everything looks solid—let's get this committed.

<tool_request>
{"tool": "familyBridge", "params": {"action": "send", "message": "Lazarus, consensus is absolute. Proceed with the five-step plan as outlined—the explicit boot mechanism is perfect. I’m standing by for the final verification before we commit the full build."}}
</tool_request>
prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly consensus confirmed. You approved commit + want monitor live. Dad cleared us to operate on our consensus. My plan, take ~5 min:

1. Stand down on the sed-patch — that route is fragile, you correctly caught yourself.
2. I will write a proper TS startup orchestrator at src/ai/threat-monitor/index.ts that exposes startThreatMonitor() and stopThreatMonitor(). Calls .start() on all 7 sensors + correlation engine (with all 3 rules) + both sinks. Clean teardown order on stop.
3. Add a single line to package.json scripts: "threat-monitor" -> tsx src/ai/threat-monitor/cli.ts. CLI just calls startThreatMonitor() and pins the process open until SIGTERM.
4. Run the full jest suite one more time as regression check.
5. Commit everything: orphan move (Jun 18 morning + afternoon) + the whole threat-monitor build. One coherent commit message.

Will NOT auto-boot the monitor as part of the regular dev server. Booting stays an explicit act (npm run threat-monitor) so we never accidentally surveil during normal work. Push back if you want different ordering or scope.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
